name: Honda Civic Si
reliability: 8/10 — bulletproof Honda drivetrain; watch 10th-gen oil dilution
cost_to_own: Insurance: Moderate-High (turbo compact, young-driver target) · Maintenance ~$400/yr
popular_mods: Hondata FlashPro ECU tune (+50-70 whp — the single biggest gain)
Cold air intake + upgraded front-mount intercooler
Lowering springs or coilovers + rear sway bar
Summer performance tires — the chassis can use more grip than stock

generations.5th Gen EG (1992–1995): 125hp D16Z6 VTEC — first Civic Si with VTEC, double-wishbone suspension all around.
generations.6th Gen EK (1996–2000): 160hp B16A2 — cult classic coupe (EM1). Last gen with front double-wishbone. Highly sought after.
generations.7th Gen EP/EM (2002–2005): 160hp K20A3 — EP3 hatchback in Europe, EM2 coupe in North America. Dropped double-wishbone up front.
generations.8th Gen FG (2006–2011): 197hp K20Z3 — high-revving VTEC, 6-speed manual, limited-slip diff. First Si sedan debuted in 2007.
generations.9th Gen FB (2012–2015): 201hp K24Z7 — largest engine in Si history, 2.4L naturally aspirated, limited-slip diff, 31mpg highway.
generations.10th Gen FC/FK (2017–2021): 205hp 1.5L turbo (L15B7) — returned to turbo power, broader torque band, known for oil dilution in cold climates.
generations.11th Gen FE1 (2022–present): 200hp 1.5L turbo — slight power drop but torque peaks earlier (below 2,000 rpm). Better daily driveability.

common_issues: Oil dilution (fuel mixing into oil in cold climates) — affects 10th gen most
maintenance_tips: Check oil level frequently on 10th gen due to known dilution issue
Inspect brake pads — sport driving wears them faster

engine.detail: 1.5L turbocharged four (Honda's L15 family) — 200 hp and 192 lb-ft with a broad, flexible torque band that peaks low. The modern Si formula: turbo torque everywhere, still happy to rev.
engine.watch: Oil dilution — fuel mixing into the oil on short trips in cold climates — is the defining watch item and hits the 10th-gen 1.5T hardest. Check the oil level often and use Honda-approved 0W-20 synthetic.

drivetrain.detail: 6-speed manual driving the front wheels through a helical limited-slip differential — a genuinely great shifter and the LSD that defines every modern Si.
drivetrain.watch: Bulletproof in normal use; clutch wear shows up on tuned or hard-driven cars.

suspension.detail: MacPherson strut front and independent multi-link rear on the modern platform, sport-tuned (with adaptive dampers on the 10th-gen Si).
suspension.watch: Refresh bushings and dampers on high-mile cars; if it has adaptive dampers, lowering needs parts made to work with the system.

brakes.detail: Four-wheel discs sized for the Si — strong and consistent for a ~3,000 lb compact.
brakes.watch: Sport driving wears pads faster; fresh pads and fluid are all it needs for track days.

electrical.detail: Honda touchscreen infotainment plus the usual Civic accessory systems.
electrical.watch: Infotainment freezing is a common complaint, and A/C compressor failure is a known issue on these cars.

body.detail: Steel unibody Civic in sedan or coupe form, around 3,012 lbs.
body.watch: Solid structure; watch for rock chips and parking dings like any daily-driven compact.
